rules.title: Ban the Box - Criminal History Inquiry Restrictions in Housing
rules.quote: Inquiry into and consideration of any applicant's criminal history shall take place only after the applicant has submitted a formal application.
rules.summary: Landlords and real estate brokers may not inquire about or consider an applicant's criminal history until after the applicant submits a formal application.
rules.coverage_text: Article does not apply to rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit, or to rental of rooms in a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to rental of a single unit in a two-family dwelling where owner occupies the other unit, or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.
rules.penalty: First violation up to $500; subsequent violations up to $1,000.

rules.title: Ban the Box - Scope of Permissible Criminal History Inquiry in Housing
rules.quote: A landlord or real estate broker shall be permitted to inquire about: Indictable offense convictions in New Jersey for eight years following the release from post-conviction custody or from the date of sentencing if the person was not incarcerated; Disorderly persons convictions or municipal ordinance violations in New Jersey for five years following the release from post-conviction custody or from the date of sentencing if the person was not incarcerated; and Pending criminal charges.
rules.summary: Landlords may inquire about indictable convictions within eight years of release or sentencing, disorderly persons convictions within five years, and pending charges, but cannot inquire about arrests that did not result in conviction, expunged records, or juvenile records.
rules.key_value: 8 years for indictable offenses; 5 years for disorderly persons offenses
rules.coverage_text: Article does not apply to rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit, or to rental of rooms in a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to rental of a single unit in a two-family dwelling where owner occupies the other unit, or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling. Murder, attempted murder, arson-related offenses, sex offenses requiring registry, and terrorism-related crimes may be considered regardless of when they occurred.
rules.penalty: First violation up to $500; subsequent violations up to $1,000.

rules.title: Ban the Box - Required Considerations of Criminal History in Housing
rules.quote: A landlord or real estate broker shall consider the following factors in evaluating the applicant and the results of any criminal history inquiry: Any information, if provided, pertaining to the degree of rehabilitation and good conduct or to the accuracy of the criminal record in question produced by the applicant; The amount of time that has passed since the conviction(s) and/or release from custody; and The nature of and circumstances surrounding the crime(s).
rules.summary: When evaluating criminal history, landlords must consider evidence of rehabilitation and good conduct, the time elapsed since conviction or release, and the nature and circumstances of the crime.
rules.coverage_text: Article does not apply to rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit, or to rental of rooms in a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to rental of a single unit in a two-family dwelling where owner occupies the other unit, or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.
rules.penalty: First violation up to $500; subsequent violations up to $1,000.

rules.title: Ban the Box - Notice Requirements After Adverse Housing Decision
rules.quote: If after conducting a criminal history inquiry the landlord or real estate broker makes a final determination adverse to the applicant resulting in the refusal of any rental, lease, assignment, or sublease, the landlord or real estate broker shall, within 10 business days Notify the applicant in writing of the adverse action, stating the reasons for rejection and including the landlord's or real estate broker's consideration of factors required under Section 2:31-4 of this Article; and Provide the applicant with a copy of the results of the criminal history inquiry.
rules.summary: If a landlord denies an application based on criminal history, they must notify the applicant in writing within ten business days, stating the reasons for rejection and providing a copy of the criminal history inquiry results.
rules.coverage_text: Article does not apply to rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit, or to rental of rooms in a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to rental of a single unit in a two-family dwelling where owner occupies the other unit, or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.
rules.penalty: First violation up to $500; subsequent violations up to $1,000.

rules.title: Ban the Box - Prohibition on Criminal History References in Housing Advertisements
rules.quote: In connection with any rental, lease, or sublease, it shall be unlawful for a landlord or real estate broker to produce or disseminate any advertisement that directly or indirectly references the use or consideration of an applicant's criminal history.
rules.summary: Landlords and real estate brokers may not produce or disseminate any advertisement that directly or indirectly references the use or consideration of an applicant's criminal history.
rules.coverage_text: Article does not apply to rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit, or to rental of rooms in a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to rental of a single unit in a two-family dwelling where owner occupies the other unit, or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling. Exception for statutory eligibility restrictions specified by law.
rules.penalty: First violation up to $500; subsequent violations up to $1,000.
